results.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Spec
results.source_text:
/-- The spectrum of a commutative ring, as a scheme.

The notation `Spec(R)` for `(R : Type*) [CommRing R]` to mean `Spec (CommRingCat.of R)` is
enabled in the scope `SpecOfNotation`. Please do not use it within Mathlib, but it can be
used in downstream projects if desired. To use this, do:
```lean
import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

variable (R : Type*) [CommRing R]

open scoped SpecOfNotation

#check Spec(R)
```
-/
def Spec (R : CommRingCat) : Scheme where
  local_affine _ := ⟨⟨⊤, trivial⟩, R, ⟨(Spec.toLocallyRingedSpace.obj (op R)).restrictTopIso⟩⟩
  toLocallyRingedSpace := Spec.locallyRingedSpaceObj R
results.docstring:
The spectrum of a commutative ring, as a scheme.

enabled in the scope `SpecOfNotation`. Please do not use it within Mathlib, but it can be
used in downstream projects if desired. To use this, do:

#check Spec(R)

results.name: Mathlib.Tactic.Ring.Common.Result
results.source_text:
/--
The result of evaluating an (unnormalized) expression `e` into the type family `E`
(typically one of `ExSum`, `ExProd`, `ExBase` or `BaseType`) is a (normalized) element `e'`
and a representation `E e'` for it, and a proof of `e = e'`.
-/
structure Result {α : Q(Type u)} (E : Q($α) → Type*) (e : Q($α)) where
  /-- The normalized result. -/
  expr : Q($α)
  /-- The data associated to the normalization. -/
  val : E expr
  /-- A proof that the original expression is equal to the normalized result. -/
  proof : Q($e = $expr)
results.docstring:
The result of evaluating an (unnormalized) expression `e` into the type family `E`
(typically one of `ExSum`, `ExProd`, `ExBase` or `BaseType`) is a (normalized) element `e'`
and a representation `E e'` for it, and a proof of `e = e'`.

results.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace
results.source_text:
/-- The Hilbert space for single-particle quantum mechanics on `Space d` with measure `μ`
  is defined to be `L²(Space d, ℂ; μ)`, the space of `μ`-a.e. equal equivalence classes
  of functions `f : Space d → ℂ` for which `∫ x, ‖f x‖² ∂μ` is finite. -/
abbrev SpaceDHilbertSpace (d : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Space d) := volume) := Lp ℂ 2 μ
results.docstring:
The Hilbert space for single-particle quantum mechanics on `Space d` with measure `μ`
is defined to be `L²(Space d, ℂ; μ)`, the space of `μ`-a.e. equal equivalence classes
of functions `f : Space d → ℂ` for which `∫ x, ‖f x‖² ∂μ` is finite.

results.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperator
results.source_text:
/-- Component `i j` of the angular momentum operator is the continuous linear map
from `𝓢(Space d, ℂ)` to itself defined by `𝐋ᵢⱼ ≔ 𝐱ᵢ∘𝐩ⱼ - 𝐱ⱼ∘𝐩ᵢ`. -/
def angularMomentumOperator {d : ℕ} (i j : Fin d) : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) :=
  𝐱 i ∘L 𝐩 j - 𝐱 j ∘L 𝐩 i
results.docstring:
Component `i j` of the angular momentum operator is the continuous linear map
from `𝓢(Space d, ℂ)` to itself defined by `𝐋ᵢⱼ ≔ 𝐱ᵢ∘𝐩ⱼ - 𝐱ⱼ∘𝐩ᵢ`.

results.name: QuantumMechanics.positionCLM
results.source_text:
/-- Component `i` of the position operator is the continuous linear map
  from `𝓢(Space d, ℂ)` to itself which maps `ψ` to `xᵢψ`. -/
def positionCLM : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) :=
  SchwartzMap.smulLeftCLM ℂ (Complex.ofRealCLM ∘L coordCLM i)
results.docstring:
Component `i` of the position operator is the continuous linear map
from `𝓢(Space d, ℂ)` to itself which maps `ψ` to `xᵢψ`.

results.name: QuantumMechanics.momentumCLM
results.source_text:
/-- Component `i` of the momentum operator is the continuous linear map
from `𝓢(Space d, ℂ)` to itself which maps `ψ` to `-iℏ ∂ᵢψ`. -/
def momentumCLM : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) :=
  (- Complex.I * ℏ) • (SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℂ (Space d) ℂ (basis i)) ∘L
    (SchwartzMap.fderivCLM ℂ (Space d) ℂ)
results.docstring:
Component `i` of the momentum operator is the continuous linear map
from `𝓢(Space d, ℂ)` to itself which maps `ψ` to `-iℏ ∂ᵢψ`.

results.name: CategoryTheory.Grothendieck.transport
results.source_text:
/--
If `F : C ⥤ Cat` is a functor and `t : c ⟶ d` is a morphism in `C`, then `transport` maps each
`c`-based element of `Grothendieck F` to a `d`-based element.
-/
@[simps]
def transport (x : Grothendieck F) {c : C} (t : x.base ⟶ c) : Grothendieck F :=
  ⟨c, (F.map t).toFunctor.obj x.fiber⟩
results.docstring:
If `F : C ⥤ Cat` is a functor and `t : c ⟶ d` is a morphism in `C`, then `transport` maps each
`c`-based element of `Grothendieck F` to a `d`-based element.

results.name: HahnEmbedding.Seed.baseEmbedding
results.source_text:
/-- Combining all `HahnEmbedding.Seed.coeff` as
a partial linear map from `HahnEmbedding.Seed.baseDomain` to `HahnSeries`. -/
noncomputable
def baseEmbedding : M →ₗ.[K] Lex R⟦FiniteArchimedeanClass M⟧ where
  domain := seed.baseDomain
  toFun := (toLexLinearEquiv _ _).toLinearMap ∘ₗ (HahnSeries.ofFinsuppLinearMap _) ∘ₗ
    (finsuppLequivDFinsupp K).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ seed.hahnCoeff

a partial linear map from `HahnEmbedding.Seed.baseDomain` to `HahnSeries`.

results.name: RigidBody.transport_law_inertial_rotating
results.source_text:
/-- For any vector field A(t), its inertial-frame time derivative equals the rotating-frame
    derivative plus the contribution from the frame rotation:
      (dA/dt)_inertial = (dA/dt)_rotating + Ω × A.
    Here Ω is the angular velocity of the rotating frame. -/
informal_lemma transport_law_inertial_rotating where
  tag := "LL36-Ltransport"
  deps := [``RigidBody]
results.docstring:
For any vector field A(t), its inertial-frame time derivative equals the rotating-frame
derivative plus the contribution from the frame rotation:
  (dA/dt)_inertial = (dA/dt)_rotating + Ω × A.
Here Ω is the angular velocity of the rotating frame.

results.name: RigidBody.transport_law_for_momentum
results.source_text:
/-- For linear momentum, the relation between inertial and rotating derivatives is
      (dP/dt)_inertial = d'P/dt + Ω × P.
    So, d'P/dt + Ω × P = F which is the linear-momentum equation in the rotating frame. -/
informal_lemma transport_law_for_momentum where
  tag := "LL32-transportP"
  deps := [``RigidBody]
results.docstring:
For linear momentum, the relation between inertial and rotating derivatives is
  (dP/dt)_inertial = d'P/dt + Ω × P.
So, d'P/dt + Ω × P = F which is the linear-momentum equation in the rotating frame.

results.name: LorentzGroup.genBoostAux₂
results.source_text:
/-- An auxiliary linear map used in the definition of a generalised boost. -/
def genBoostAux₂ (u v : Velocity d) : Vector d →ₗ[ℝ] Vector d where
  toFun x := - (⟪x, u.1 + v.1⟫ₘ / (1 + ⟪u.1, v.1⟫ₘ)) • (u.1 + v.1)
  map_add' x y := by
    rw [← _root_.add_smul]
    apply congrFun (congrArg _ _)
    have hx := Velocity.one_add_minkowskiProduct_ne_zero u v
    field_simp [add_tmul]
    simp only [map_add, add_apply, neg_add_rev]
    ring
  map_smul' c x := by
    rw [map_smul]
    simp only [FunLike.coe_smul, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, RingHom.id_apply]
    rw [smul_smul, mul_div_assoc, neg_mul_eq_mul_neg]
results.docstring: An auxiliary linear map used in the definition of a generalised boost.

results.name: LorentzGroup.genBoostAux₁_toMatrix_apply
results.source_text:
lemma genBoostAux₁_toMatrix_apply (u v : Velocity d) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    (LinearMap.toMatrix Vector.basis Vector.basis (genBoostAux₁ u v)) μ ν =
    η ν ν * (2 * u.1 ν * v.1 μ) := by
  rw [LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, basis_repr_apply]
  simp only [genBoostAux₁, LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk, minkowskiProduct_basis_left, apply_smul]
  ring
